That's exactly what I wanted, and the little plain-language readout under the box — "text contains Rome, and either tag articles or tag books, and exclude travel" — is genuinely reassuring, because I can double-check it did what I meant before trusting the results.

I especially like the honest example you slipped in: the "bookseller's guide" that has the word "books" sitting in its description but not as a tag got correctly left out. That's the exact distinction I was worried about — I want a tag to mean the label I stuck on, not just the word appearing somewhere. Good.

One question that comes straight out of this, since you've made "and / or / not" into special words: what happens the day I actually want to search for one of those words itself? Say I saved something with "Law and Order" in the title, and I just type that phrase — I wouldn't want it treating "and" as a command and getting confused. Is there a way for me to say "no, I mean the literal words" — like putting quotes around a phrase to search it exactly as written? If I can do that, the search is complete for me.
